title: Consent, belongings and decision authority
audience: Coordinators, support workers and trained cleaners who may be asked to work in a home affected by hoarding or environmental neglect, as part of an authorised support plan. Not a qualification or authority to clear a property, dispose of a resident's belongings, enter by force, or provide welfare or clinical support.
learningOutcomes: Match each proposed action to a specific, current consent for a named area, action and item.
Use the four decision categories (retain, relocate, undecided and authorised disposal) in an item-decision log.
Pause and record a contested removal instead of acting on a third party's request.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers consent and the recording of decisions about belongings. It does not give legal advice on who may decide in a tenancy, guardianship or other arrangement, and it does not authorise the disposal of anyone's property. Those questions depend on the law that applies, and the coordinator confirms the position before any disposal.

instruction.heading: Consent is specific
instruction.body: Consent must be specific to the area, the action and the possession. Access to a home, a key, or a family member's wish is not blanket permission to dispose of its contents. The WA Department of Health guidance on help with hoarding advises getting the person's permission before touching or removing their things, and notes that a written agreement with the cleaning service can set out which items will be removed. Use that as the baseline: the agreement names the items, and anything not named stays where it is. Consent can also be withdrawn, and a withdrawal stops the action at once.

instruction.heading: The item-decision log
instruction.body: Keep an item-decision log with four categories: retain, relocate, undecided and authorised disposal. Each entry records the item or its location, the decision, who made it and the date. Let the resident revisit decisions. An undecided item is never treated as disposal-ready because it is in the way. If a relative asks the crew to discard sealed boxes while the resident is away, the relative does not hold that decision. Pause the handling, leave the boxes where they are, record the request, and seek a valid, documented decision from the resident or from the person the support plan names.

procedure: Confirm the resident's current consent for the specific area and action before touching any item.
Open the item-decision log and record each item as retain, relocate, undecided or authorised disposal.
Date and attribute each decision to the person who made it.
Leave undecided and contested items in place. Do not move them to make the work easier.
If a third party asks for an item to be removed, pause, record the request and refer it to the coordinator.
Confirm the disposal list with the resident before anything leaves the home.

workedExamples.situation: A relative asks the crew to discard sealed boxes while the resident is away.
workedExamples.reasoning: Pause. The relative does not hold the decision, and access to the home is not consent to dispose of belongings. Leave the boxes in place, record the request and seek a valid, documented decision from the resident or the person the support plan names.

workedExamples.situation: The resident agrees that the kitchen bench may be cleared. Boxes beside the bench are not mentioned.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the boxes go with the bench?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Consent is specific to the item. The boxes are undecided, so they stay in place, are recorded as undecided, and are revisited with the resident at the next visit.

equipmentAndPpe: Item-decision log with the retain, relocate, undecided and authorised-disposal categories.
Labelled holding areas for each category, agreed with the resident.
Training-only mock log entries. No real belongings are handled in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Treating access to the home as permission to clear everything.
commonErrors.prevention: Limit work to documented, specific and current consent. Refer any broader demand.

commonErrors.error: Disposing of an undecided item because it is in the way.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep undecided items where they are, record them and revisit the decision with the resident.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a relative's or manager's choice about the resident's possessions.
commonErrors.prevention: Pause, record the request and obtain the resident's dated decision.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consent is specific to the area, the action and the possession, and it can be withdrawn. Access to a property is not consent to dispose of its contents.
Who may decide when a tenancy, guardianship or other arrangement is involved depends on the law that applies, which this lesson does not set out. Check it with the coordinator before acting.
Completing this lesson does not give authority to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings.

qualityStandard: The learner matches each action to a specific, current consent and refuses any action outside it.
The learner uses the four decision categories and records who decided and when.
The learner leaves undecided and contested items in place and records the request.
documentationEvidence: Item-decision log with the four categories, dated and attributed.
Record of each third-party request and the referral made.
Consent record for each area and action.
summary: Consent is specific: area, action and possession.
Access and keys are not consent to dispose of belongings.
Undecided items stay where they are.
Contested removals are paused and referred.

knowledgeChecks.question: A resident agrees that the bathroom cabinet may be cleared. A box on the bathroom floor is not mentioned. What should happen to the box?
options: Remove it with the cabinet contents, because it is in the same room.
Photograph it and put it in general waste.
Leave it in place, record it as undecided and revisit it with the resident.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about a relative's request to discard belongings is correct?
options: The request is paused and recorded, and the resident's dated decision is obtained.
The request is enough if the relative holds a key.
The request is accepted if the resident cannot be reached quickly.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does each entry in an item-decision log need to record?
options: Only a photograph of the item.
The item or its location, the decision, who made it and the date.
The price of the item and its resale value.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a home by force, to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings without valid consent, to handle or dispose of hazardous waste, to deal with unstable stacks or structural hazards, or to provide welfare, clinical or safeguarding assessments. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Work is done only under an authorised support plan and a written agreement with the resident, within the limits set by the employer and the local law. Tenancy, safeguarding and information-sharing rights are jurisdiction-specific, and fire-risk, structural, pest and hazardous-waste decisions belong to the competent authorities and specialists named in the plan. Where authority or consent is unclear, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: consent is not specific, documented and current; the resident has objected or withdrawn consent; a party seeks entry by force, nonconsensual disposal or removal of personal documents; a fire-load, ignition, egress or obstruction hazard is present; a stack or structure is unstable; pests, unknown liquids or mouldy goods are present; sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are found; waste would go to general disposal without characterisation; private information is requested without authority; or the work would go beyond the approved plan. Stopping is a valid professional outcome. Record the disagreement, protect the resident's choices and refer the authority dispute before any property is moved.
